Header: Gibberella fujikuroi (syn. Fusarium moniliforme ) Foot rot/Dhanko fhed kuhine rog

Prevention: Rotate all types of rice with crops other than cereals (e.g. vegetables) for 2 seasons as the disease can survive on crop debris or in soil.
Agrovets as the disease can develop in seeds.
For non-certified seed, soak the seeds in hot water at 60 degrees
C for 10 minutes before sowing to reduce seed infection and disease incidence in nurseries and fields.
Avoid overuse of nitrogenous fertilizer (more than 100 kg/Ha) causing too vigorous plant growth that favours the disease.
Burn plant residue with known infection in fall season.
Monitoring: It is seen mostly during the rainy season.
Infected plants become elongated, thin, slightly yellow and produce less tillers compared with healthy plants.
Monitor the nursery once a week as well as the main field for 40 days after transplanting.
As the disease progresses, development of foot rot and aerial roots from the upper nodes of the stem.
Check for white/pink fungal growth on lower parts of dying plants.
Consider control measures when disease is first seen in the nursery or the primary field.
Direct Control: Uproot and destroy infected plants from the nursery (bury 50cm deep or burn outside of field).
Soil drenching with biopesticide products prior to planting or during transplantation, e.g.
M5), multi-site action, contact (protectant), broad-spectrum fungicide.
Restrictions: Alternate fungicides to avoid disease resistance.
When using a pesticide or botanical, always wear protective clothing and follow the instructions on the product label, such as dosage, timing of application, PHI, max number of sprays, REI.
Do not empty into drains and water sources.
